format: lightsuffer-ios slice6 stochastic effects fixture v1

notes.float_format: all floating point values are rounded to 7 significant digits
notes.grain: the grain of the negative (spektrafilm.model.grain.apply_grain) is measured on the difference between the cmy_film tap with and without the grain: it is the grain field itself, in density units.
notes.glare: the glare of the print (spektrafilm.model.glare.add_glare) is measured on the difference between the rgb_out tap with and without the glare: it is the visible effect of the glare, in the encoded sRGB domain. The upstream does not apply any glare to a directly scanned film, so the glare of the slide is not applicable.
notes.seeds: the upstream grain reseeds the global NumPy random state with a fixed seed (0, 1, 2 per channel, plus ten per sub layer), so the upstream grain is deterministic. The fixture shifts those seeds (by 1000 * (seed + 1)) to measure the spread of the upstream; the algorithm is not touched. The upstream glare draws from the unseeded global random state, so the fixture seeds it.
notes.fast_aggregate: the same grain runs with the fast samplers of the upstream (spektrafilm.utils.fast_stats, settings.use_fast_stats = True). The Swift port reproduces those samplers, so this is the closest reference for the port; the difference between the two aggregates measures the error of the normal approximation the fast samplers use.
notes.film_format: the grain is the shot noise of the silver halide grains a pixel holds: its amplitude scales with one over the square root of the number of particles per pixel, i.e. with the area of the pixel. The cases therefore use a 1 mm film format (a pixel of 15.6 um on a 64 x 64 image), so that the grain is visible.
notes.statistics: mean_c and std_c: the mean and the standard deviation of the field of the channel c. acf_l: the autocorrelation of the centred field at the lag l (the horizontal and the vertical neighbours pooled). corr_i_j: the correlation of the channels i and j. qXX: the quantiles of the density histogram (the three channels pooled).

images.description: flat: a flat mid grey patch (0.18). textured: a vertical ramp, a noise floor (numpy default_rng(20261111)) and two saturated patches.
